data.narrative:
Parallel Systems, a Series B transportation frontier-tech company founded by Matt Soule, John Howard, and Ben Stabler, has raised $100M to date. The transportation sector peer set includes seven private companies (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, DeepDrive among others) and no public comparables, limiting traditional peer benchmarking.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The Stage-Progression method uses a $25M proxy derived from total capital raised and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B step-ups, implying a valuation of $48M. Peer-Median analysis was not viable; while three transportation peers exist in the data set, none met narrow-filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) with sufficient count to support median benchmarking. Using an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable error given the sector's heterogeneity.

The triangulation yields a median valuation of $48M, with a low-end floor of $40M and high-end ceiling of $55M. This range reflects stage-appropriate growth from the total-raised baseline but carries material uncertainty. The absence of same-stage transportation comparables and reliance on a single methodological pillar mean the valuation is sensitive to the base-raised proxy assumption and step-up multiplier calibration. External validation through expanded peer data or revenue/margin benchmarking would strengthen conviction in this range.
